Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury with Mr. Salahuddin Dolon -- For petitioner
Mr. Mad Hossain Chowdhury -- For Respondent No. 1 
Mr. Md. Asadullah -- For Respondent No. 3
parties:
M. Shamsul Haque ----- Petitioner
Versus
Bangladesh Export Processing Zone Authority and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The writ petitioner applying against a public advertisement  for the post of Manager under the Bangladesh Export Pressing Zone Authority (BEPZA) and through interview got appointment with effect from 29.10.92 and that the Respondent No. 3 was appointed within out advertisement and without having requisite qualification for the office of Manager with effect from 16.3.93. Accordingly, the Respondent No. 3 was junior to the writ petitioner in the service of BEPZA. The Respondent No. 3 was neither appointed under the provisions of the Defence Services Officers (Appointment and Fixation of Seniority in Civil Post) Rules, 1983 (hereinafter referred to as the Rules, 1983) nor appointed as per provisions of the Bangladesh Export Processing Zone Authority Employees Rules, 1990 (hereinafter referred to as the Rules 1990) as he did not have required qualification. In the Gradation list dated 25.11.96, the Respondent No. 3 was shown as senior to the petitioner since he was allowed the benefit of the Rules, 1983. The Respondent No. 3 was promoted to the post of Deputy General Manager vide letter dated 30.1.1997 and the Respondent No. 3 joined the said the office on 5.2.97. The petitioner was subsequently on 6th May 1998 promoted to the post of Deputy General Manager. The petitioner on 27th December, 1998 submitted a representation to restore his seniority over the Respondent No. 3 stating that the Respondent No. 3 was not appointed under the Rules, 1983, on which the Respondent No. 1 formed a committee to examine his claim and the said committee submitted its report on 17.2.2000 holding amongst others that the petitioner is senior to Respondent No. 3 and that the appointment of the Respondent No. 3 was not inconformity with the Rules, 1999 of  BEPZA and or the Rules, 1983 and recommended for preparation of a new seniority list for the purpose of promotion putting the joining date as the effective date but the said recommendation has been set aside without any reason and the Respondent No. 1 has now taken steps to give promotion to the Respondent No. 3 to the office of General Manager and that the Respondent No. 1 decided to maintain the impugned seniority list to the grave prejudice to the petitioner and under such circumstances the petitioner caused issuance of Demand Justice Notice and there being no response, the petitioner moved this writ petition and obtained the instant Rule. 

 3. The Respondent Nos. 1 and 3 entered appearance separately by filing separate powers and separate affidavits-in-opposition containing more or less similar statements. In the affidavit-in-opposition it is stated that the Respondent No. 3 is a Commissioned Officer and he was appointed by the Respondent No. 1 under the provision of Rules, 1983 on 16.1.93 in the post of Manager and as per Rule-5 of the Rules, 1983 the period of his service under the Defence Service has been added with the Service under BEPZA for consideration of seniority and accordingly the gradation list, showing seniority of the officers, was published on 25.11.96 and objection were invited, if any, against the aforesaid gradation list, allowing time up to 25.12.96, but there was no objection filed and accordingly the aforesaid gradation list made final and in the said gradation list it was mentioned that the seniority of the Respondent No. 3 has been calculated giving him benefit as per Rules, 1983 and subsequently the Respondent No. 3 was given promotion to the post of Deputy General Manager on the basis of the said gradation list on 30.1.97 and thereafter the petitioner was promoted to the post General Manager on 6.5.98 as per Rule 3(6) read with Rule 14 of the Rules, 1990 and that the Respondent No. 3 joined the post of Deputy General Manager on 5.2.97 and the petitioner having joined the Office of Deputy General Manager on 6.5.98, the Respondent No. 3 became senior in the said grade i.e. in the office of the Deputy General Manager and that the statement made in the writ petition that a committee was constituted by the Respondent No. 1 on receipt of the  representation of the petitioner dated 27.12.98 is not correct and that the petitioner's service in the Bangladesh Small and Cottage Industries Corporation could not be added with his present service in the absence of backing of law and that the period of service of the Respondent No. 3 in the Defence Service has been Added with his present service BEPZA in terms of the Rules, 1983. It has been stated that the Armed Forces Division by a letter, dated 3.10.93 requested the Establishment Division to provide appointment to three (3) retired officers of the Army including the Respondent No. 3 and accordingly, the Establishment Division by its letter dated 17.10.92 forwarded the names of said Army Officers to the Respondent No. 1 and thereafter the Respondent No. 3 also approached the Respondent No. 2 for his appointment and that the pay scale and position of the post of Manager in BEPZA and that of Major in Bangladesh Army being more or less equal, the Respondent No. 1 gave appointment to the Respondent No. 3 in the post of Manager and the Executive Board of BEPZA in its meeting held on 31.8.96 granted the seniority to the Respondent No. 3 as per Rules, and accordingly, the gradation list showing seniority of the class one officers was prepared and circulated inviting objection, against the seniority shown and accepted the said gradation list and that thereafter the petitioner did not raise objection against the promotion of the Respondent No. 3 when made and thereby the petitioner gave away his right of seniority, if any, over the Respondent No. 3 and that in the post of Deputy General Manager, the Respondent No. 3, is senior to the petitioner and has acquired a vested right and therefore the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 4. Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioner challenged the vires of Rules, 1983 contending amongst others that the Defence Service Officers (Appointment and Fixation of Seniority in Civil Posts) Rules, 1983, was not made under any parent law and as such it has no legal basis after the revocation of the Martial Law, though it appears that the protection has been given by sub-clause 6 of paragraph 19 of the fourth schedule of the Constitution. The provisions of said Rules, 1983 being violative of equality clause and ex facie discriminatory and it is also void being inconsistent with the provisions of Chapter-III of the Constitution as has been mandated under Article 7(2) and 26 of the Constitution and that the provisions of the Rules, 1983 are contrary to the basic structure and fundamental right guaranteed under the Constitution and that the sub-clause 7 of paragraph 19 of Fourth Schedule of the Constitution provides that the Constitution shall stand fully revived and restored and subject to the provisions of said paragraph have the same effect and operate as if it had never been suspended and therefore the then Chief Martial Law Administrator, did not have any power under any law to make the impugned Rules, 1983 and therefore the Rules 1983 is inconsistent with the provisions of the Constitution. 

 5. Mr. Md. Asadullah, the learned Advocate, appearing for the Respondent No. 3, submits that it had already been settled both by the High Court Division and the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh that the Rules, 1983 is a valid law and in support of his contention, the learned Advocate referred to the decision in the case of AYBI Siddiqui Vs. Government of Bangladesh reported in 21 BLD (HC) 75 and Lt. Col. (Rtd.) Nazimuddin Ahmed Vs. Bangladesh reported in 1995 BSCR (Vol-8) page 95, wherein it has been held that the Rules, 1983, promulgated by the Chief Marshal Law Administrator in pursuance of the Promulgation of the 24.3.82 was protested when the Martial Law was lifted with effect from November 10, 1986 by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1986 with the addition of paragraph 19 to the Fourth Schedule in the Constitution, wherein sub-paragraph 6 provides that "All Ordinance and other laws in force immediately before the date of commencement of the said Act shall subject to the proclamation revoking the said proclamation and withdrawing the Martial Law, continue in force until altered, amended or replaced by competent authority". The learned Advocate further submits that Article 150 of the Constitution also approves the validity of the Rules, 1983. 

 8. Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury, the learned Advocate, then submitted that the petitioner has been discriminated in that the Rules, 1983 is applicable amongst the same class of army officers in view of the word inter se as appearing in the Rules and therefore the Respondent No. 3 being an Army Officer cannot be equated with the writ petitioner, who is a Civil Officer, in a such as they did not come from the same service. The learned Advocate then submits that the writ petitioner was appointed on 29.10.92 whereas the Respondent No. 3 was appointed on 16.1.93 and therefore ex facie the Respondent No. 3 is junior to the writ petitioner in the service in BEPZA as per Rules, 1990 of BEPZA which provides that person appointed in the cadre earlier will get seniority as per Rule 13 of the Rules, 1990. The learned Advocate taking us through the paragraph No. 3 of the affidavit-in-reply to the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition dated 17.3.2002 and Annexure-G to the affidavit-in-reply to the affidavit-in-opposition of the Respondent No. 3 dated 8.11.2001, which is the appointment letter of the Respondent No. 3, submits that no where in the appointment letter of Respondent No. 3 it has been mentioned that the Respondent No. 3 has been appointed under the Rules, 1983 and on the contrary it appears from the plain reading of the appointment letter dated 5.12.92, that the appointment of Respondent No. 3 has been made on his own approach and that the said letter contains the terms of the appointment of the Respondent No. 3 which the Respondent No. 3 accepted and confirmed in writing, and that.;3 he was required to procure health certificate from the Civil Surgeon and his appointment was subject to furnishing of such certificate. The learned Advocate taking us through the provisions of the Rules, 1983, copy of which has been annexed as Annexure-A to the writ petition, submitted that no appointment to a Civil Post under the said Rules. 1983 is given without a recommendation of the competent authority and that the terms and condition of service of a defence service officer shall be similar to those applicable to other incumbent to the Civil Post and that clearance from Service Head Quarters is required. But there was no such clearance from the Defence Service Head Quarter in case of the Respondent No. 3. The learned Advocate referred to the paragraph 17 of the affidavit-in-opposition of the Respondent No. 3 and paragraph 16 of the affidavit-in-opposition of Respondent No. 1 and submitted that Establishment Division enquired from BEPZA whether posts are available for appointment of three Army Officers, but the BEPZA did not reply to the same and no material could be placed before the Court to show that the Establishment Division sent necessary papers of Respondent No. 3 to the BEPZA for his appointment in the post of Manager, rather the appointment letter dated 5.12.92 shows that the appointment of Respondent No. 3 was made on the personal approach of the Respondent No. 3 and on the basis of an interview and therefore it cannot be said that the appointment was made under the Rules, 1983, consequently the seniority given to the Respondent No. 3 on the basis of Rules, 1983 is without lawful authority. The learned Advocate further submitted that at the time of gradation list was published, the petitioner believed that the Respondent No. 3 was appointed under the provisions of Rules, 1983 as has been mentioned in the gradation list and there was no reason to disbelieve the information disclosed by ,BEPZA but after the pro- motion of the petitioner in the post of Deputy General Manager he came to know that the appointment of the Respondent No. 3 was made on the personal approach of the Respondent No. 3 and not on the basis of Rules, 1983 and hence at the earliest opportunity the writ petitioner raised objection through his representation. The learned Advocate, referring to Annexure-D and E to the writ petition and the statements made in paragraph 7 of the affidavit-in-reply to the affidavit-in-opposition of Respondent No. 3 dated 8.11.2001 submitted that in response to his objection, the authority formed a committee to examine the allegations and the said committee found that the appointment of Respondent No. 3 was made without any proper either recommendation from the Defence Ministry or the Establishment Division and the appointment was made without any advertisement, and that the said committee recommended to give seniority to the petitioner over the Respondent No. 3, but for reasons best known to the authority the said recommendations have not been implementation. The learned Advocate, submits that the aforesaid Annexure-G and the statements made in paragraph 7 of the affidavit-in-reply dated 8.11.2001 have not been denied or controverted and therefore the same are to be treated as true and correct. The learned Advocate then submitted that the question of waiver and estoppel does not arise in the case in as much as the writ petitioner bonafide believed the contents of the gradation list that the Respondent No. 3 has been given the seniority in terms of Rules, 1983 and the writ petitioner could know about the fact that the Respondent No. 3 was not entitled to the benefit of seniority under the Rules, 1983 since not appointed under the provisions of Rules, 1983, only after his promotion to the post of Deputy General Manager and accordingly the writ petitioner registered his objection as aforesaid at the earliest. 

 9. Mr. Md. Asadullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the Respondent No. 3 submitted that as per law the authority having allowed time to raise objection against the gradation list within a specific time and the writ petitioner having failed to raise objection there against and there after the Respondent No. 3 having been given promotion on the basis of said gradation list and at that time also there being no objection raised by the writ petitioner and the objection having raised by the writ petitioner only after his own promotion to the post of Deputy General Manager such objection could not be said to be bonafide and is hit by the principle of acquiescence, waiver and estoppel. In support of his contention the learned Advocate referred to the decisions in the case of Ashok Kumar Vs. Collector reported in AIR 1980 (SC) 112 and in the case of Akhlesur Rahman and others Vs. Safurullah and others reported in 14 BLD(AD) wherein it has been held that in case of inordinate delay writ petition is not maintainable and that acquiescence and waiver operates as estoppel against the writ petitioner. The Respondent No. 3 being otherwise qualified for promotion has been discharging his functions as Deputy General Manager and thereby he acquired a legal-right and that the waiver being abandonment of a right, the petitioner now cannot challenge the seniority and/or the promotion of the Respondent No. 3 on the basis of the gradation list. The learned Advocate referred to a decision in the case of Rasha Lal and others Vs. National Board of India and others reported in 1980 (Supp) SCR 449 and submitted that the reopening the question of legality of an appointment after several years cannot be said to be justified. In the said case the appointment of respondents were made when there was no sanction for such post and the respondents were irregularly appointed that the respondents were appointed in 1975 and the writ petition was filed in 1978 and because of such delay their Lordships have held that it would not be justified reopening the case of the respondents after several years of their appointment. The learned Advocate also referred to the decision in the case of B.V.S. Sivaiash and others Vs. Addarki Babu and others reported in AIR 1998 (SC) 2565 wherein it has been held that there is merit in the contention that since there was no challenge to the promotion made on 3rd May, 1993 and the promoted petitioner had been working for 5 years by then and acquired right to the seniority of such promotion and they could not be deprived and the High Court in our opinion, has rightly held that the objection as to the validity of the promotion made on 3rd May, 1993 as raised by the appellant in the appeal cannot be entertained and therefore liable to be dismissed. The learned Advocate submits that in the facts that the gradation list was published on 25.11.96 and thereafter the Respondent No. 3 was given promotion on the basis of said gradation list on 31.9.97 and the alleged objection has been raised on 27.12.98 and that too after the promotion of the petitioner on the basis of the same gradation list, on 6.5.98 and therefore with passage of time the Respondent No. 3 has acquired right to seniority and in fact the Respondent No. 3 in now senior to the petitioner is the grade because of his longer stay in the position of Deputy General Manager and therefore the Rule is liable to be discharged Mr. Md. Salahuddin DoIon, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury referred to a decision in the case of P.K. Ram Chandra Iyer Vs. Union of India reported in AIR 1984 (SC) 541 and submitted that the decision referred to by the learned Advocate for the Respondent No. 3 reported in AIR 1980 has been reversed. The learned Advocate relying on the said AIR 1984-decision submitted that once it is established that the appointment was made contrary to the Rules and in violation of the requirement of qualification, the appointment is required to be quashed and set aside. 

 10. Mr. Asad Hossain Chowdhury, the learned Advocate, appearing for the Respondent No. 1 submitted that the appointment of Respondent No. 3 was made as per practice and custom of BEPZA and that the Respondent No. 3 is discharging his functions in accordance with law since 1993 and that he was promoted to the post of Deputy General Manager without any objection and the writ petitioner being promoted to the post of Deputy General Manager in 1998, the writ petitioner became junior to the Respondent No. 3 at least in the grade of the Deputy General Manager as per Rule 13 of the Rules, 1990. The learned Advocate also adopted the submissions and arguments made by the learned Advocate for the Respondent No. 3. 

 11. We have perused the writ petition, affidavits-in-opposition and the supplementary affidavits. We have perused the decisions cited and considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates of the respective parties. In view of the Appellate Division's decision that the Rules, 1983 is a valid law, we are bound by the said decisions reported in 21 BLD (HCD) 75 and 1995 BSCR (Vol-8) 95, Considered the provisions of Rules, 1983 and the statements made in paragraph 16 of the affidavit-in-opposition of Respondent No. 1 and paragraph 17 of the affidavit-in-opposition of the Respondent No. 3 and the Annexure-G to the affidavit-in-reply dated 8.11.2001 to the affidavit-in-opposition of the Respondent No. 3 dated 13.8.2001 and it appears that the appointment of Respondent No. 3 has not been made as per Rule, 1983 but is an independent appointment on the basis of an application made by the Respondent No. 3 in his personal capacity and on the basis of an interview and since the appointment of the Respondent No. 3 has not been made under Rule, 1983, he is not entitled to get the benefits under the aforesaid Rules, 1983. In this connection the decision in the case of Lt. Col. (Rtd.) Nazimuddin Ahmed Vs. Bangladesh reported in 1995 BSCR (Vol. 8) page 95 is applicable, wherein it has been observed that The appellant's last ditch argument that he could well be appointed under the Rules. 1983 has got little substance. The quotation of consideration of regularization and absorption of his service in terms of the said rules does not arise as he was already is on contract basis in terms of Section 6(1) of the Ordinance, 1985. There was no reference to 1983 Rules in any of the orders passed with regard to his appointment in the Corporation. His terms and conditions of service are to be guided by Season 6(1) of the Ordinance of 1985, under which is appointment was made. In the instant case we found that the appointment of the Respondent No. 3 was not made under the Rules, 1983 and the Rules, 1983 is not applicable in his case and he is not entitled to get any benefit under Rules, 1983. Accordingly the seniority given to the Respondent No. 3 in the gradation list was illegal and without any lawful authority and the writ petitioner being appointment earlier in the post of manager he is senior to Respondent No. 3 as per Rule, 1990. We however do not find any material or criteria to the allegation of discrimination as has been made by the writ petitioner. In the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of our above findings we need not go to examine the meaning of "inter-se" as appearing in the Rules, 1983 in as much as this rule can be disposed of without examining the same. 

 12. We find substance in the explanation given by the learned Advocate for the petitioner as to the delay in raising objection against the seniority of the Respondent No. 3. There is no reason to disbelieve to the information given by the authority like BEPZA. In giving seniority to the Respondent No. 3 the BEPZA di sklosed that the appointment of Respondent No. 3 was made as per provisions of Rules, 1983, which the writ petitioner has found to be incorrect only after this promotion to the post of Deputy General Manager and thus it cannot be said that the writ petitioner was negligent on acquiesced and or waived, his right to object and therefore estopped from challenging the seniority given without lawful authority to the Respondent No. 3. Having regard to the decisions in the cases reported in AIR 1980 (SC) 449 and AIR 1998 (SC) 2565 with which we respectfully agree, we find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the Respondent No. 3 that the Respondent No. 3 having functioning and continuing in the post of Deputy General Manager for a pretty long time, he has acquired a legal right. The decision reported AIR 1980 (SC) 449 has been reversed by the decision reported in AIR 1984 (SC) 541 but the relevant reasoning appears to us as to be acceptable. 

 14. Accordingly the Rule is made absolute in part without any order as to costs. It is declared that the provisions of Rule 5 of the Defence Service Officers (Appointment and Fixation of Seniority in Civil Posts) Rules, 1983 is a valid provision of law and that the petitioner is senior to the respondent No. 3 in service with Bangladesh Export Processing Zone Authority (BEPZA) and that the promotion of the Respondent No. 3 to the post of Deputy General Manager is not to be disturb and that the petitioner shall get preference ahead of the Respondent No. 3 for consideration, in case of promotions, in future.
